title: Probability-Conserving Flow Guidance
claim: Under strong guidance the baseline oversaturates and hallucinates artefacts, while our method yields cleaner, more realistic samples from the same prompts and seeds.
layout: 2x3 image grid, rows labeled baseline vs ours, top-to-bottom comparison
description: A 2-row by 3-column grid of generated photographs with no arrows or diagrams. The row label on the left of the top row reads 'CFG' and the bottom row reads 'Ours (AdaMaG)'. Each column uses the same prompt and seed. Column 1 is a wooden sailboat on turquoise water. Column 2 is a woman in a yellow dress and sun hat walking through a golden wheat field. Column 3 is two blue hyacinth macaws against a green background. The CFG row looks oversaturated and has artefacts: a distorted boat with a flat sky, a woman with a smeared hat and dress, and macaws with merged, malformed beaks. The AdaMaG row looks more natural and detailed, with a flag and wake on the boat, flowing hair and dress on the woman, and clearly separated macaws with sharper eyes and beaks. The eye goes first to the vivid, saturated images, then compares the rows vertically.
caption: AdaMaG vs. CFG. CFG (top) vs AdaMaG (bottom), same prompts and seeds. CFG shows saturation and hallucinated artefacts that grow with guidance scale; AdaMaG limits departure from the learned density path at the same scale, yielding cleaner generations with no inference overhead.
abstract: Diffusion and flow-based generative models dominate visual synthesis, with guidance aligning samples to user input and improving perceptual quality. However, Classifier-Free Guidance (CFG) and extrapolation-based methods are heuristic linear combinations of velocities/scores that ignore the generative manifold geometry, breaking probability conservation and driving samples off the learned manifold under strong guidance. We analyse guidance through the continuity equation and show its effect decomposes into a divergence term and a score-parallel term defined invariantly across parameterizations. We prove the divergence term blows up structurally as sampling approaches the data manifold, motivating a time-dependent schedule alongside score-parallel attenuation. The resulting plug-and-play rule, Adaptive Manifold Guidance (AdaMaG), targets both terms at no additional inference cost. Finally, we show that several existing saturation and manifold preserving heuristics can be read as acting on one of these two terms. On image generation benchmarks, AdaMaG improves realism, reduces visible artefacts, and induces controlled desaturation under strong guidance.
